key_insight: Laser post-treatment reduced wear rates by approximately 24% for detonation-sprayed coatings and 39% for gas-flame-sprayed coatings, with deposition-dependent changes in hardness and elastic modulus.
engineering_relevance: Laser post-treatment offers a route to improve the wear resistance of Ni–Cr–Fe–Si–B–C coatings on AISI 321 stainless steel.
method: Deposit coatings by detonation spraying and gas-flame spraying, then apply laser post-treatment.
Compare microstructure and phases using SEM, EDS and XRD.
Measure hardness, elastic modulus and dry-sliding performance using indentation and ball-on-disk tests.
evidence_signal: After treatment, wear rates fell from 1.939 to 1.465 × 10⁻⁴ mm³/(N·m) for detonation-sprayed coatings and from 2.419 to 1.476 × 10⁻⁴ mm³/(N·m) for gas-flame-sprayed coatings.
watch_item: Treatment must be tailored to the deposition method: gas-flame-sprayed coatings showed improved wear resistance but a decrease in elastic modulus from 228.0 to 187.0 GPa.
paper_title: Effect of Laser Post-Treatment on the Microstructure, Mechanical and Tribological Properties of Detonation- and Flame-Sprayed Ni–Cr–Fe–Si–B–C Coatings
